images.title: Squares sit inside rectangles
images.purpose: Shows that a 4 cm by 4 cm square belongs inside the set of rectangles, next to a 5 cm by 2 cm rectangle that is not a square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large oval with a smaller oval inside it, each holding one small shape.
images.exact_structure: One large horizontal oval outlined in teal (#0072B2), labelled Rectangles at its top edge. Inside it, on the right, a smaller oval outlined in reddish purple (#CC79A7), labelled Squares at its top edge. In the left part of the big oval (outside the small oval) one rectangle in dark outline, 5 by 2 in proportion, lightly filled teal, with the label 5 cm under its bottom side and 2 cm beside its right side. Inside the small oval one square in dark outline, lightly filled reddish purple, with the label 4 cm under its bottom side and 4 cm beside its right side. Each shape has a tiny right angle mark in one corner. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square has all angles 90°, so every square is also a rectangle.
images.description: Shows that a 4 cm by 4 cm square belongs inside the set of rectangles, next to a 5 cm by 2 cm rectangle that is not a square.
images.context: All four figures have all angles 90°, so all are rectangles; only 4 cm by 4 cm has equal sides.

image_decisions.why: The nested ovals show that the square is a special rectangle, using the concept's own sizes.
